title: GoHighLevel Pricing 2026: $97–$497 + Hidden Costs
description: Starter $97, Unlimited $297, Agency Pro $497/mo — plus the SMS, email and AI usage costs nobody lists, and what actually lands on your first invoice.
html_content:
GoHighLevel costs $97/month (Starter), $297/month (Unlimited), or $497/month (Agency Pro, which most people call SaaS Pro). Annual billing knocks roughly 17% off any tier — HighLevel charges 10 months for 12, so two months are free. The $497 tier's official name is Agency Pro; plenty of people call it SaaS Pro because it's the plan that unlocks SaaS Mode. Same plan, same price. That's the headline. But the plan price isn't the whole bill: SMS, email, and AI usage are billed on top, and most pricing articles skip that part. I've run GHL for agencies long enough to know exactly what lands on your first real invoice. This is the straight breakdown for 2026 — plan prices, wallet usage and the main published add-ons, re-checked against HighLevel's own pricing and billing documentation in August 2026.

Pricing is only half the money question. For the other half — how to actually accept payments inside GoHighLevel — see the full payments overview.

Once you’ve picked a plan, the next step is connecting a payment processor in GoHighLevel so you can start collecting money.

Want to see your real costs before paying anything? Start the extended 30-day free trial — double the standard 14 days, $0 to start — just a ~$1 card-verification hold.

Quick Answer: GoHighLevel Pricing in 2026

GoHighLevel has three plans, all billed monthly with no per-user fees:

  • Starter — $97/month. The full platform for a single business.
  • Unlimited — $297/month. Unlimited sub-accounts, white-label, API. The agency plan.
  • Agency Pro — $497/month. Everything in Unlimited plus SaaS billing and usage rebilling.

Annual billing saves about 17% on every tier. There's no permanent free plan, but there is a 30-day free trial (extended from the standard 14) with $0 to start — just a ~$1 card-verification hold. SMS, email, and AI are usage-based costs billed on top of your plan. The rest of this guide breaks down exactly what that means for your wallet.

The Three GoHighLevel Plans

GoHighLevel keeps it simple with three tiers. No confusing add-on bundles, no per-seat pricing games. You pick a plan, you get the tools. Here's what each one actually gives you.

Starter — $97/month

The Starter plan is built for solo operators and small agencies that need the core CRM, pipeline management, and automation tools without sub-account reselling. You get the full suite of features: funnels, websites, email marketing, calendars, workflows, reputation management, and the conversation inbox. It's everything you'd need to run a single business from one dashboard.

What you don't get: unlimited sub-accounts, white-labeling, or the ability to resell GHL as your own SaaS product. If you're using GHL for your own business or running a lean operation, Starter covers it.

Not sure Starter is enough? Try the full platform free for 30 days — full access, $0 to start, just a ~$1 card-verification hold. Test it before you pick a plan.

Unlimited — $297/month

This is the agency plan. Unlimited sub-accounts means you can onboard as many clients as you want without per-account fees eating into your margins. You also get branded desktop apps, custom domains, and API access that lets you build integrations specific to your agency's workflows.

Most agencies land here. Once you're onboarding multiple clients, you'll want the unlimited sub-accounts and white-label that Starter doesn't include — and you stop worrying about account limits as you grow. Unlimited also unlocks advanced reporting, custom menu links, and the ability to white-label the entire platform under your own branding.

Most agencies land here. Start the extended 30-day free trial and onboard a real client before you commit to $297/month.

Agency Pro (SaaS Pro) — $497/month

Agency Pro is for people who want to sell GoHighLevel as their own software product. You get everything in Unlimited plus automated SaaS billing through Stripe, a built-in SaaS configurator for setting up pricing tiers, and usage-based rebilling so you can pass SMS and email costs through to your clients with markup.

The real value here is the rebilling infrastructure. Instead of eating usage costs yourself, Agency Pro lets you set per-message and per-email rates for your clients. If you're running a white-label SaaS business on top of GHL, this plan pays for itself quickly.

Want to test the rebilling setup yourself? Start your 30-day free trial — double the standard 14 days, and you can cancel any time.

Hidden Costs Nobody Talks About

Your plan price is just the platform fee. The real variable cost comes from usage. Here's what actually hits your invoice on top of your monthly plan:

USAGE-BASED COSTS

  • SMS: ~$0.015 per outbound text message (inbound is also charged)
  • Email: $0.675 per 1,000 emails sent, the same rate on every plan (about seven hundredths of a cent each, not a cent)
  • AI Features: Metered pricing based on model and usage — conversation AI, content generation, and AI employees all consume credits
  • Phone Numbers: Local numbers run a few dollars per month each; toll-free numbers cost more
  • Call Minutes: Inbound and outbound calling is billed per minute on top of your plan
  • Premium Actions: Some workflow actions and A2P 10DLC registration carry additional fees

For a typical small agency sending a few thousand texts and emails per month, expect usage costs roughly in the $30–$150 range on top of your plan fee. High-volume operations with heavy SMS campaigns can see usage costs that rival or exceed the platform fee. The point is to understand this before you commit — GHL is transparent about these charges once you know where to look, but the marketing pages don't lead with them. The cleanest way to know your real number is to run a normal week inside the free trial and watch the usage meter.

One more cost that only applies to some agencies: if you serve healthcare clients whose patient data lives in GoHighLevel, the HIPAA add-on is $297/month on top of any plan — and it can never be cancelled once enabled. What the Agency Wallet Actually Pays For

Usage does not land on your plan invoice. It comes out of a separate Agency Wallet: you load it, HighLevel draws it down as you use things, and when it drops below a threshold your card is charged again to top it up. Wallet credit cannot pay your subscription, and your subscription does not cover usage. Two different bills, and the second one is the one that surprises people.

HighLevel's billing documentation names these as the common wallet-funded services — the list is explicitly not exhaustive, so treat it as the floor:

  • the Phone System — numbers, calls, SMS and MMS
  • the Email System — sends, including emails carrying video
  • Email Validation
  • AI usage
  • Autocomplete Addresses
  • Workflow Premium Features — premium actions and webhooks, at $0.01 per execution

That last line settles a question people ask constantly: a workflow firing 11 premium actions costs 11 cents, not a subscription. A third-party dialer wired in through a premium action bills the same way, per execution, not as a monthly fee.

Phone and SMS rates are Twilio's rates, and they vary by country. That is why nobody publishes a single number: a text to a mobile in the US, India, Nigeria or Germany is four different prices. Your own rates show in the sub-account billing screen before you send anything.

Agent Studio is not included in any plan — it stays pay-per-use on every tier. AI Studio and Ask AI were free under the Summer of AI promotion. HighLevel states that post-promotion charges apply beginning 1 September 2026, so if you have been trying those features free this summer, check your wallet from that date rather than assuming they stayed free.

Outside those subscriptions, AI is token-metered. Reviews AI and Content AI are included on the AI Employee plans subject to their limits; the published pay-per-use and overage rates are Reviews AI at $0.01 per review, Content AI at $0.063 per image and $0.0945 per 1,000 words, Voice AI from $0.045 per minute for the voice engine, with text-to-speech and model tokens on top. Bring your own model (Gemini, GPT, Claude) and you pay that model's rates.

Domains bought through HighLevel are charged yearly at the registrar price, not monthly, and renew like any other domain.

What GoHighLevel Replaces (the Comparison That Matters)

The honest way to judge GHL's price isn't against a single competitor — it's against the stack it replaces. Most agencies and small businesses pay for several separate tools that each do one job. GoHighLevel rolls them into one flat fee with no per-seat charges:

Add up what you'd pay for even three or four of those tools separately — depending on the tools and your team size, those subscriptions can rival or exceed GHL's flat fee, and most of them charge per seat while GHL doesn't. That's the real reason agencies move to GHL: one bill, one login, and no per-user tax as your team grows. Whether it's worth consolidating depends on whether you'll actually use the breadth (more on that below).

Annual vs Monthly: Is the Discount Worth It?

GoHighLevel offers annual billing that saves roughly 17% compared to paying monthly. On the Starter plan, that works out to about $970 per year instead of $1,164 — saving you around $194 annually. The same percentage applies across all tiers.

My recommendation: start monthly. Use the 30-day trial first, then run month-to-month for at least 2–3 months until you're confident GHL is your long-term stack. Once you know you're staying, switch to annual and bank the savings. There's no penalty for starting monthly and switching later.

Quick Math

Starter annual: ~$970/year ($81/month effective) — about $194 back vs monthly. Unlimited annual saves roughly $594/year, and Agency Pro close to $1,000/year. Meaningful money on the higher tiers.

The Truth About GoHighLevel Promo Codes & Discounts

Let me save you 20 minutes of Googling: there is no working GoHighLevel promo code for an ongoing discount on your monthly subscription. Every coupon-aggregator site listing "GHL codes" is outdated, fabricated, or just redirects you to the standard signup page with no discount applied. GoHighLevel's pricing is set — $97 / $297 / $497 — and they don't undercut it with floating promo codes.

The legitimate ways to pay less are simple and they're all real: the extended 30-day free trial (a full extra month of free access), annual billing (~17% off), and the occasional seasonal promotion GHL runs directly around Black Friday and summer. That's it. For the full breakdown of every legitimate way to save, see our GoHighLevel free trial & discounts guide.

Which Plan Should You Choose?

Choose Starter ($97/month) if: You're running a single business, you're a freelancer managing a few clients, or you're testing whether GHL fits your workflow before scaling. Starter gives you every core tool — CRM, funnels, automations, calendars, email. You just don't get unlimited sub-accounts or white-labeling.

Choose Unlimited ($297/month) if: You're an agency with more than 3 clients, you need white-label branding to present GHL as your own platform, or you want API access for custom integrations. The unlimited sub-accounts alone make this the obvious pick for anyone running a real agency.

Choose Agency Pro ($497/month) if: You're building a software business on top of GHL. You want to charge your clients their own subscription fees through Stripe, rebill usage costs with markup, and operate a fully white-labeled SaaS product. If that's not your model, you don't need Agency Pro.

Most people reading this should start with the 30-day trial on Starter, then upgrade to Unlimited once they're onboarding clients. That's the common path for GHL agencies.

Is GoHighLevel Worth It?

GHL is worth it if you'll actually use the breadth. The value isn't "a cheaper CRM" — it's replacing 4–10 separate subscriptions with one flat fee and no per-seat charges. If you're currently paying for a CRM, an email tool, a funnel builder, a scheduler, and a texting front-end, GHL almost always nets out cheaper and removes the glue work of syncing them.

It's not worth it if you only need one of those jobs done. If all you want is a simple email list or a single landing page, GHL is more platform than you need and a dedicated tool will be simpler. The honest test: list what you pay for today, add it up, and compare. Then use the free trial to confirm the workflows actually hold up for your use case before you commit a dollar.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does GoHighLevel cost?

GoHighLevel costs $97/month for Starter, $297/month for Unlimited, and $497/month for Agency Pro. Annual billing saves about 17%. SMS, email, and AI usage are billed separately on top of the plan fee.

Is there a free plan for GoHighLevel?

No. GoHighLevel does not offer a permanent free plan. But you can get a 30-day free trial (extended from the standard 14 days) to test the full platform before paying anything. $0 to start — just a ~$1 card-verification hold.

What's the cheapest GoHighLevel plan?

The cheapest plan is Starter at $97/month ($81/month effective on annual billing). There is no tier below $97. To pay less per month than $97, your only lever is annual billing — promo codes for ongoing discounts don't exist.

Can I get GoHighLevel cheaper than $97/month?

Only through annual billing, which brings Starter down to roughly $81/month (about $970/year). Outside of occasional seasonal promotions run directly by GHL, no promo code or negotiation gets you below the standard monthly rate.

What's included in each plan?

All three plans include the core CRM, pipelines, funnels, websites, email, SMS, calendars, workflows, and reputation management. Unlimited adds unlimited sub-accounts, white-labeling, and API access. Agency Pro adds Stripe SaaS billing and usage rebilling on top of everything in Unlimited.

Does GoHighLevel charge per user?

No. GoHighLevel does not charge per seat or per user. Your plan covers the platform and you can add team members without additional per-user fees — one of the main reasons agencies prefer GHL over per-seat tools.

Are SMS and email costs included in the plan price?

Not entirely. The plan gives you platform access, but SMS (~$0.015 per outbound segment, Twilio's rate for your country), email ($0.675 per 1,000 sent), and AI usage are billed separately based on consumption. Think of GHL like a utility: the plan is your base, usage is variable on top.

Is there a GoHighLevel promo code or coupon?

No working promo or coupon code exists for an ongoing subscription discount. Codes listed on coupon-aggregator sites are fake, expired, or redirect to the standard signup. The real ways to save are the extended 30-day trial, annual billing (~17% off), and seasonal promotions GHL runs directly.

Does GoHighLevel do Black Friday deals?

Yes. GoHighLevel has historically run Black Friday and Cyber Monday promotions, typically a discount off the first few months. These are announced through GHL's official email list and social channels — no coupon code required; the discount is applied during the promotional window.

How much is GoHighLevel in India / in rupees?

GoHighLevel is priced in US dollars globally — $97 / $297 / $497 per month — so the cost in India is the USD price converted at the current exchange rate plus any card forex fees your bank charges. There is no separate discounted India plan.

Can I downgrade or cancel my plan?

Yes. You can downgrade (Agency Pro → Unlimited → Starter) or cancel at any time from your billing settings. Downgrading from Unlimited to Starter limits sub-accounts and removes white-labeling, so plan the transition before you switch.

Is GoHighLevel worth the price?

It's worth it if you'll use the breadth — replacing several separate subscriptions (CRM, email, funnels, scheduling, texting) with one flat fee usually nets out cheaper and removes integration headaches. It's not worth it if you only need one of those jobs done. Use the free trial to confirm before committing.

Is there a setup fee, deposit, or minimum contract?

No. The three standard plans have no setup fee, no deposit, and no minimum term — you are billed monthly (or annually) and can cancel from billing settings. The only setup charge HighLevel publishes is Advanced Account Setup at $1,000, which is an optional done-for-you service, not something applied to a normal signup. Starting the trial does require a card, which carries a ~$1 card-verification hold that is released, not charged.

What is the difference between the three GoHighLevel plans?

The plans (sometimes called tiers or packages) split on how many businesses you run and whether you resell. Starter $97 gives you up to three sub-accounts and the core CRM, funnels, calendars and reputation tools. Unlimited $297 removes the sub-account cap and adds white-labeling and API access. Agency Pro $497 — the tier most people call SaaS Pro — adds SaaS Mode, Stripe SaaS billing and usage rebilling on top of everything in Unlimited. Usage is billed separately on all three.

What do premium workflow actions and webhooks cost?

Workflow Premium Features are wallet-funded and billed at $0.01 per execution. So a workflow that fires 11 premium actions or webhooks costs about 11 cents each time it runs, not a monthly fee. Free workflow tools exist alongside them with daily limits.

Does GoHighLevel bill in euros, rupees, or local currency?

HighLevel prices in US dollars everywhere — $97 / $297 / $497 — so a buyer in the eurozone, India, Africa or anywhere else pays the USD price converted by their card issuer, plus any foreign-transaction fee the bank adds. There are no separate regional plans. Phone and SMS usage is the exception that genuinely differs by country, because those follow Twilio's per-country rates.
